decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm side approach to holder in right workspace, gradually selecting elbow-up configuration; pens will be handled by left.
Advance right arm toward holder, finishing inward-facing horizontal side grasp orientation; maintain left arm at origin.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller translation and yaw increments to preserve right-arm joint continuity.
Pause yaw near wrist singularity and translate forward slowly, seeking a continuous elbow-up approach.
Continue open side approach toward holder at estimated table height, retaining the nonsingular wrist orientation.
Align right gripper around holder body and close; retention will be checked visually during a cautious lift.
Maintain closed right gripper and lift holder slowly toward the central right workspace; verify it follows the hand.
Holder did not follow lift. Reopen and realign farther forward around its observed body before retrying grasp.
Fine-adjust holder grasp forward and slightly outward, close fully, then test retention with a short vertical lift.
Holder tipped during failed grasp. Withdraw upward open, then begin a top-down recovery approach while keeping elbow configuration continuous.
Replan recovery with substantially smaller wrist increments after continuity rejection, lifting clear of the fallen holder.
Rotate right gripper toward a downward grasp over the fallen holder; use corrected table-plane estimate and small approach increments.
Halve rejected rotation and translation increments to preserve joint continuity during downward reorientation.
Retract from reach limit and yaw toward a front-facing recovery approach, maintaining the existing elbow-up branch.
Use very small retraction and yaw increments after rejection to move away from the kinematic boundary.
Approach the fallen holder with a more downward-facing open gripper, lowering the wrist to retain reach margin.
Stop wrist rotation after guard interruption and make a small positional alignment toward the near end of the fallen holder.
Retract from the reach boundary and yaw toward a forward-facing recovery grasp rather than extending the elbow further.
Reduce retreat and yaw increments to one third after zero-step rejection, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Continue turning the gripper forward and aligning laterally with the fallen holder while staying inside the recovered reach margin.
Advance and square the jaws across the fallen holder body, then close for a recovery grasp; retention remains uncertain.
Test recovery grasp with a slow lift and retraction, keeping the right gripper fully closed and watching for holder motion.
Holder remained on table beyond fingertips. Reopen and approach lower and farther forward, using wrist view to align its near end.
Advance the open jaws another two centimeters around the holder's near body and close without lifting yet.
Withdraw clear and rotate toward a top-down grasp to avoid pushing the holder farther away with the fingertips.
Back away from the reach boundary, lowering and leveling the right gripper for a horizontal grasp of the fallen holder.
Reduce the rejected retreat and leveling increments to preserve joint continuity near the boundary.
Continue leveling the open right gripper and lower toward a horizontal recovery grasp, now away from the joint boundary.
Level the jaws horizontally at the fallen holder's body height and advance to straddle its sides rather than contact its top.
Close around the now-centered holder body and perform a short lift/retraction to check retention.
Lift and retract with the holder clamped, beginning to rotate its long axis upright; verify which end is open.
Previous lift was empty. Return with open horizontal jaws, aiming lower around the fallen holder's actual body rather than its upper edge.
Lower the horizontal jaws to the middle of the fallen holder and close only after straddling its sides.
Allow jaws to finish closing at the lower body height, then make a small straight lift and retraction to verify retention.
Holder now follows the gripper. Keep it clamped, retract into reachable workspace, and raise the far/open end toward upright.
Continue bringing the retained holder upright and closer to the central right workspace, keeping its mouth reachable by the left arm.
After the tracking-related continuity interruption, rotate the retained holder upright with much smaller increments while slowly retracting.
Pause rotation at the wrist limit. Lift and retract the held holder at fixed orientation to regain joint margin before uprighting.
Retract and raise the holder further to free wrist pitch travel; begin the left arm's continuous elbow-up preparation for pen handling.
Raise/retract the retained holder while uprighting; simultaneously move the left arm above the pens with a downward grasp orientation.
Complete upright holder rotation with extra wrist clearance; align left gripper above the nearer purple pen without closing yet.
Release the now-upright empty holder to settle vertically for a side regrasp; lower the left gripper onto the purple pen's center.
Correct left grasp using wrist view and close on purple pen; return right hand toward fallen holder for a lower, mouth-up recovery.
Lift and begin uprighting the first pen while bringing the right hand back to a horizontal recovery approach at the holder's new location.
Finish holding the pen vertically. Lower right jaws around the fallen holder; its opening appears to face the robot, so recovery rotation must raise that near end.
Replan below the wrist pitch limit by tilting the right jaws slightly down and lowering in small increments. Keep the first pen closed and upright.
Right hand met contact before its target. Replan from actual pose, shift left to center the holder and lower gently at the observed horizontal orientation.
Clear the obstructed side approach upward and turn the right gripper toward a top-down grasp of the holder; keep the pen retained.
Halve the rejected lift and wrist rotation increments, starting from the unchanged observed pose.
Continue rotating the open right hand downward above the holder, compensating forward to keep its fingertips over the body.
Finish top-down alignment over the holder's midpoint and offset slightly right to clear its upper edge before closing.
Holder shifted nearer the robot. Translate the downward open gripper over its newly observed midpoint, then lower slightly to straddle it.
Center the downward jaws slightly nearer over the holder and close around its full body width; keep the pen retained in the left hand.
Lift the clamped holder and yaw its opening toward the center, preparing an inward side-hold uprighting motion instead of exceeding wrist pitch.
Holder visibly retained with its opening at the near end. Finish yawing the mouth inward before lifting it upright by a transverse rotation.
Raise the inward-facing holder mouth using a transverse rotation while moving the retained pen toward a central overhead insertion approach.
Continue uprighting the retained holder with its mouth visibly inward/upward; align the first pen over its eventual opening without releasing.
Finish making the holder upright, correct the pen's visible lean, and lower it toward the mouth while both grasps remain closed.
Move the first pen slightly left to center it over the upright holder and lower its bottom into the opening; hold right arm steady.
Release the first pen inside the upright holder and withdraw the left hand upward and left; keep holding the holder securely.
First pen is visibly retained in the holder. Move the open left hand toward the remaining purple pen while rotating into a downward grasp.
Holder slipped onto the table but remains upright with one pen. Reorient the right jaws for a conventional side regrasp while approaching the second pen with the left.
Clear the left hand away from the displaced holder before any further descent; continue right wrist roll at a safe stand-off distance.
The holder is now in the left workspace. Use the left arm to recover it from above while the right hand retreats and finishes leveling its side-grasp orientation.
Stop right-arm motion after the continuity interruption. Center the left downward gripper over the fallen holder and lower to its body height.
Contact shifted the holder. Align the left jaws across its new diagonal axis and move nearer over its midpoint before descending further.
Close the centered left jaws on the holder, then test retention with a small lift and begin yawing its mouth toward the center.
Lift the retained holder clear and yaw its far/open end inward, keeping the left elbow-up and the right arm stationary.
Finish yawing the held holder mouth toward the center while retracting into a comfortable left-arm reach for uprighting.
Raise the holder's open end with a transverse rotation while drawing the left wrist leftward to keep separation from the right gripper.
Complete uprighting the holder while lowering toward a stable table placement; retain the already inserted pen.
Replan with one-third pitch increments after the continuity guard; gently lower the retained holder and bring its axis nearer vertical.
Bring the right open gripper to the holder's opposite lower side for a supported handoff, leaving the left hand closed and stationary.
Stagger the right grasp below the left fingers, advance around the holder's lower body, and close for a supported handoff.
Release the left grasp and withdraw it clear while the right hand stays closed around the holder's lower body; check that the handoff retains it.
Shift the securely clamped holder into the right workspace and begin an overhead approach to the second purple pen with the left arm.
Zero-step rejection: reduce the left translation and pitch increments and introduce yaw first to avoid the wrist singularity.
Continue left-arm downward reorientation toward the remaining purple pen, holding the upright holder steady in the right hand.
Finish the downward approach to the remaining purple pen, centering the open left jaws over its middle while keeping the holder stationary.
Use small wrist-view corrections toward the pen on the left of the camera, keeping orientation fixed near the reach boundary.
Retract from the extension limit and use a shallower downward approach; the pen shifted during contact, so reassess before closing.
Zero-step rejection: reduce the retreat and shallowing motion to quarter-size increments from the unchanged observation.
Recover away from the extended configuration with gradual retraction and steeper downward orientation; switch to a nearer pen if the far pen remains inaccessible.
Reverse the last unhelpful retreat and shallow the wrist gradually to recover the prior continuous approach configuration; holder remains clamped.
Use a very small shallowing and lowering adjustment rather than further reach, watching the left configuration and pen alignment.
Lift the left hand clear at fixed orientation and shift outward slightly to recover a safer continuous configuration before another pen approach.
